### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `34a2d175ba1993d7fc4401cd6cac67f17d6a2304` — the merge of head `e84915df95f561a7a9b57598ff75d4bd1a119d0c` into base `d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 34a2d175ba1993d7fc4401cd6cac67f17d6a2304 && git checkout 34a2d175ba1993d7fc4401cd6cac67f17d6a2304
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef e84915df95f561a7a9b57598ff75d4bd1a119d0c && git checkout -B drift-repro d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef && git merge --no-ff e84915df95f561a7a9b57598ff75d4bd1a119d0c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e84915df95f561a7a9b57598ff75d4bd1a119d0c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/spec/scripts/lib/skill-map-guards.ts

Inputs read: card #33020 (body and all 5 comments: triage 6844423823, added nit 6846941860, claim 6880781482, amendment 6880933599, os-dev-report 6881607020), PR #33368 (body, 8-file list, net diff against merge-base `24f2f401`), and the check-runs on this head: 68 total, 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending (read 2026-11-14T18:05Z). The skipped ten are opt-in or not-applicable lanes (Lint UI, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood shard template, UI Published Artifacts, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, the two queue verdicts, Schedule gate). The rest of the diff (the two test files, `authorable-surface/automation.json`, `content/docs/references/automation/execution.mdx`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`ExecutionStepLogSchema` gains optional `warnings: string[]` and `droppedFields: DroppedFieldsEvent[]`: right.** The card offers declare or project out and leaves the choice to the spec lane; the seat chose declare (claim 6880781482). Types match the producer on `main`: `NodeExecutionResult.warnings` / `StepLogEntry.warnings` are `string[]` (`engine.ts:437`, `:1124`), `droppedFields` is `DroppedFieldsEvent[]` (`engine.ts:447`, `:1132`), and both in-tree writers produce exactly that (`crud-nodes.ts:782-784`, `:934-936`; `notify-node.ts:1308`). The element is the exported `DroppedFieldsEventSchema`, imported, no second copy.
- **Published responses that widen with it: right, and complete.** `ExecutionStepLogSchema` is embedded only by `ExecutionLogSchema.steps` (`execution.zod.ts:399`); `ExecutionLogSchema` only by `ListRunsResponseSchema.data.runs` and `GetRunResponseSchema.data` (`api/automation-api.zod.ts:832`, `:871`). No other reference in `packages/` or `apps/`.
- **New import edge `automation/execution.zod.ts` to `data/data-engine.zod.ts`: right.** No cycle: `data-engine.zod.ts` imports `filter`, `query`, two `data/` helpers, `shared/retired-key`, `kernel/execution-context.zod` and `shared/lazy-schema`, none of which reaches `automation/`. The member is built inside the `lazySchema` closure, the same way `foldDropEvents` and `automation-api.zod.ts` already consume the event schema.
- **Accept set, read as a parser: widened for every value the engine's typed contract produces; narrowed at one edge the PR does not name.** See N1 in ④.
- **Producer accept set (`stepAdvisoriesOf`): right.** What reaches a step is now the declared shape or nothing; in-tree producers are unchanged (their events round-trip `safeParse` to an equal object).
- **`TRANSITIVE_ALLOWLIST['objectstack-automation']`: right.** The 17 rows are byte-for-byte the 17 entries under "Transitive dependencies" in `skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md` on `main`, so the published index does not move and no governed path is in the file list (Governed Surface Queue Guard: success).

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening), on the PR body and on the changeset body; `Metadata-protocol: added` on both.

- `@objectstack/spec` minor: matches. Two optional members on a published response schema, and the `authorable-surface/automation.json` shard moves, which the Post-Task Checklist step 3 rule prices at `minor` at least. Check Changeset: success. The step log is not something a metadata author writes (the body's own `Skills-docs:` line says so), so `added` here is the gate's reading of the moved shard, not a new authorable key; the amendment 6880933599 records that, and the gate verdict governs.
- `@objectstack/service-automation` patch: matches. A fix in what the engine persists from a host executor's off-shape result; no export, type or config surface moves (`stepAdvisoriesOf` is module-local).
- No `skip-changeset`, no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- **Deviation: claim carried `Metadata-protocol: none`, PR carries `added`.** Answered: amended by the seat in 6880933599 before the report; consistent with the gate.
- **Deviation: file surface widened to `authorable-surface/automation.json` and `skill-map-guards.ts`.** Answered: same amendment; the first is generated, the second is judged in ④ and holds.
- **Deviation: `warnings` filter taken under the bounded in-place exemption.** Answered: accepted in 6880933599; same file, same defect class as nit 6846941860, and it is what makes the step parse under the schema this PR declares.
- **Deviation: `main` not merged before opening.** Answered: the head's check-runs are green on the merge ref; no changed path moved on `main`.
- **Out-of-scope finding, `carrier: none`: `builtin/region-index-keys.test.ts` pins `StepLogEntry` against `ExecutionStepLog` for the region keys only, and its comment (line 58) names `warnings` as an engine-local field the contract does not carry.** Confirmed in the live tree; that sentence is false once this PR merges. Escalated, not accepted as carrier-less: see N3.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally: answered by CI (all build and lint lanes success on this head).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts` (hits).** Holds against the card and against its first consumer. The card's scenario: a reader that parses a run through the published schema loses both members and cannot tell a step that partially did not land from a clean one. After the diff, `ExecutionLogSchema.steps` keeps both (pinned in `execution.test.ts`), and the engine's real step parses under the schema (pinned through `engine.listRuns` in `run-dropped-fields.test.ts`, including the in-tree `update_record` control). The `.describe()` text agrees with the producer: `warnings` on a `success` step is exactly what `crud-nodes.ts` and `notify-node.ts` emit; "the per-step source the run's terminal answer is folded from" is `dropEventsOf(steps)` in `run-dropped-fields.ts:24`. Attempts to break it: an import cycle (none), a second producer that writes either member onto a step past the guard (none: the only other writer is `creditChildRun`, `run-resume.ts:803-806`, which writes the output of `foldDropEvents`, well-typed by construction), a `reason` the event schema lacks (shared with every other response that already embeds the event; no new exposure).

**`packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts` (implementing).** Agrees with the contract, sentence by sentence, with one inexact sentence (N2). Both step pushes go through `stepAdvisoriesOf`; `Array.isArray` replaces the truthy-`length` test, so a string or an array-like no longer reaches the step; `droppedFields` uses the same `DroppedFieldsEventSchema.safeParse` per element as `foldDropEvents` and pushes `parsed.data`, so unknown keys on a host event are stripped too; an empty result omits the member. Key order on the step is unchanged (`warnings` then `droppedFields`). This discharges the card's added nit 6846941860 at the write.

**`packages/spec/scripts/lib/skill-map-guards.ts` (implementing).** Holds. The row follows the file's own stated rule (an allowlist row publishes on existence; a new pointer joins by a row, not by an import edge) and the `objectstack-api` precedent. It prunes the five pointers the new edge would add and admits none; verified against the index on `main` (17 of 17).

Findings:

- **N1 (nit).** The changeset's sentence "Nothing that parsed before is refused" is not exact. On a non-strict object an undeclared key was stripped whatever its value; declared, an off-shape value is refused. A step persisted before this change with `warnings: 'text'` or a malformed `droppedFields` (the old truthy-`length` copy persisted exactly those; the PR's own third service test builds one) parsed before and is refused now, and `run-history.ts:287` / `:311` serve persisted steps as stored, so the write-time guard does not reach rows already in history. Graded nit, not should-fix, because it needs a host-registered executor that violated the typed `NodeExecutionResult` contract, on a run persisted before the upgrade, read by a parser that no in-tree consumer runs (no runtime `ExecutionLogSchema.parse` outside tests); `droppedFields` has been on the step only since PR #33007. Disposition: one clause on the changeset prose naming the edge, or an accepted deviation. A serve-time filter would be a separate card and is not owed here.
- **N2 (nit).** The `stepAdvisoriesOf` docblock says the step and the answer "can never disagree about which events were real". A host event with `fields: []` is well-typed under `DroppedFieldsEventSchema` (no minimum), so the step keeps it, while `foldDropEvents` drops empty-field events (`run-dropped-fields.ts:68`). The step still parses and no in-tree producer emits an empty event, so there is no effect on correctness. It sits in a code file: accepted deviation, or folded into the N3 follow-up; not fixed on this head.
- **N3 (nit, from ③).** `region-index-keys.test.ts:58` goes stale with this PR, and the type-level pin does not yet hold `warnings` / `droppedFields` in step between `StepLogEntry` and `ExecutionStepLog`. The runtime pin in this PR (the engine's step parses under the schema) covers today's shape; the type pin is what would catch drift. Disposition: the seat files a follow-up card (reader `domain:server`, p3) to extend the pin and correct the comment; `carrier: none` is not a resting state.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Nits alone end the round.
